I too will try other flavors. This is a yummy cookie

clause: Made these a couple of times now, and I must say that they are DELICIOUS!
review:
Made these a couple of times now, and I must say that they are DELICIOUS! I used a hugarian paprika that we get from a local goulash restaurant, and baked the pecans at 350' for five minutes instead of 375' (this was because the other recipe I was making called for a 350' oven)
Cooking them slightly lower seems to have yeilded a nice pecan-caramalized, spicy, sweet, and just a little tender even after cooling.
Last night I made these in a craving, but discovered part way through that I had only half of the cider vinegar needed. It was suggested that I use some of the cheap sake we had around the house, and so I did. Turned out good, but definitely is better with full cider.
Thanks for posting!
~~Luna

I made it this past weekend as a test to see if I liked it. Well it passed the test! The color is such a beautiful ruby red and it's moist and has wonderful flavor. In fact, it tasted even better the second day so I would recommend making it the night before you need it. In making the frosting, I found the microwave was the best way to melt the marshmallows.

Beware bakers, don't make the same mistake we made. My family recommended next time to slowly melt it in a pot on the stove. Off to the grocery store again. :-/

clause: I must confess I've now been found guilty as charged.
review: I must confess I've now been found guilty as charged. I've made this recipe 4 times in 3 weeks and hadn't reviewed it till now. The first time I made it, It barely made it out of the oven when I had to have a bite, well that bite turned into lunch and an early dinner for me, I couldn't stop eating it. We have Corona bottles, so beer was out of the question. I subed a half can of a foil covered Pepsi ( wasn't sure about the colours of the can affecting it in anyway, punched a hole through the foil on the opening of the can to let the steam out, added some garlic cloves too. Unfortunately, my DH missed that one, the second and third cooking he also missed, my best friend and I devoured them. Darn, the bad luck for him..hehehe. The fourth time he made it home for a wing and part of a breast. Guess who, after eating those small pieces went to the store and bought 4 whole chickens. He now wants at least one to himself..hahahahah. I'm make him one this weekend. I promise. I baked them using a foil lined pan for no clean up and sliced them right on the can, so easy, they literally sliced right off. Thank you for such a great recipe !!!

clause: I'm a pumpkin fan, so when I saw this recipe I had to try it.
review: I'm a pumpkin fan, so when I saw this recipe I had to try it. I halved the butter, added extra pumpkin mix and then added olive oil and water in at the end to compensate for the butter liquid. Since I changed the proportions so much, I'm not going to rate this with stars, but it was good. I'd leave out the brown sugar next time because it was on the sweet side. Thanks for a nontraditional recipe using pumpkin pie mix!

clause: I made Kittencals Italian Tomato Pasta Sauce and Parmesan Meatballs https://www.food.com/recipe/kittencals-italian-tomato-pasta-sauce-and-parmesan-meatballs-71273 (the best ever) 2 days ago and we were craving meatball subs.
review: I made Kittencals Italian Tomato Pasta Sauce and Parmesan Meatballs https://www.food.com/recipe/kittencals-italian-tomato-pasta-sauce-and-parmesan-meatballs-71273 (the best ever) 2 days ago and we were craving meatball subs. I used Kittencals parmesan meatballs and Italian pasta sauce in this recipe and this was absolutely the most divine meatball sandwich ever. The addition of mayo, cream cheese and spice spread supercharged the meatball sub to a 5-star sandwich. This will be in our rotation after making Kittencals sauce and meatballs but I can understand the spread used on this sandwich would make store bought sauce and meatballs into a divine meatball sandwich. My tweak is I wrapped the bread in foil and baked at 300, for 25 minutes because we don’t like super crispy bread that crumbles when you hold it and the inner bread really infused with sauce and gooey cheese lusciousness! Our preference for cheese is the mild flavor and melty texture of monterey jack. Thank you Jaime Renee for posting a keeper for sure!

I am freezing the left overs to serve with fruit for a quick breakfast.

I only used about 1/3 lb pepperoni on top. We loved the way it got crispy. A great recipe, and everyone took leftovers for lunch the next day. Thanks.

clause: This was a huge hit, even with my raw-vegan friend!
review: This was a huge hit, even with my raw-vegan friend! We've had hot days and today hit 108?, so I opted to adjust this recipe for the crock pot. I used ground turkey instead of beef. I cooked the turkey, bacon and the veggies per instructions, threw everything else in the crock pot, and then spent the rest of the day in the pool. Everyone really enjoyed this recipe. The bacon sets it apart from other spaghetti sauces, and the only thing I'd change is to add about a teaspoon of sugar next time. Thanks for sharing this recipe, Papa D. Made and enjoyed for the 2012 Cookathon in memory of Papa D.

clause: This pie is simple, easy and it's yummy.
review:
This pie is simple, easy and it's yummy. That's what pies should be. I used 3 cups of each and added a tablespoon extra of cornstarch like other reviews suggested. The rhubarb and strawberry measurements would change depending on how sweet your strawberries are. If I had strawberries that were super sweet I would've stuck to the 4 to 2 ratio. So, taste your strawberries before you make this pie.
My pie set up really well. I don't think I needed the extra tablespoon. It doesn't hurt though. For anyone experiencing runny pies you have to let it cool for at least 4 hours. If I want my pie to set up perfectly I never cut into it before the 4 hour mark. Most fruit pies need that time. I tend to bake them the night before and let them rest while I'm asleep so I don't have the urge to cut into it.
My only other suggestion would be to add more cinnamon. I'll bake it a second time and probably add 1/2 tsp. If that's still not enough I would add 3/4 tsp and so on until it had enough for my taste.

This pie is simple, easy and it's yummy. That's what pies should be. I used 3 cups of each and added a tablespoon extra of cornstarch like other reviews suggested. The rhubarb and strawberry measurements would change depending on how sweet your strawberries are. If I had strawberries that were super sweet I would've stuck to the 4 to 2 ratio. So, taste your strawberries before you make this pie.
My pie set up really well. I don't think I needed the extra tablespoon. It doesn't hurt though. For anyone experiencing runny pies you have to let it cool for at least 4 hours. If I want my pie to set up perfectly I never cut into it before the 4 hour mark. Most fruit pies need that time. I tend to bake them the night before and let them rest while I'm asleep so I don't have the urge to cut into it.
My only other suggestion would be to add more cinnamon. I'll bake it a second time and probably add 1/2 tsp. If that's still not enough I would add 3/4 tsp and so on until it had enough for my taste.

clause: Delicious!!
review: Delicious!! This is a wonderful way to use up the abundance of cherry tomatoes, basil, and oregano that my garden is producing. I used 4 cups of "Juliet" cherry tomatoes (which are a grape shaped cherry tomato), that I cut in half. Also, I used 4 cloves of garlic instead of 2 cloves. Juliet cherry tomatoes are a little bigger, so I needed to bake these closer to 3 hours before turning the oven off to cool. I packed half of the recipe in a jar with olive oil and put in the refrigerator. The other half was put in a baggie and stuck in the freezer. Sun-dried tomatoes are so expensive to buy in the store, so I was thrilled to find this easy, economical and very delicious way to get the same thing. Thank you so much for posting this fantastic recipe...it is definitely a keeper!!

clause: Another awesome recipe from my hero Alton!
review: Another awesome recipe from my hero Alton! I've made this recipe so many times and it continues to come out wonderful. I even went to gluten free and used gluten free flour and ground flax meal instead of wheat germ. I've used it with firm tofu too, just mixed it extra long to break up the bits. I've subbed different dried fruit including flaked coconut. I even subbed a 1/4 cup of chocolate chips for part of the fruit just to add a small reward for eating healthy. I cut the slab into 16 pieces and put each in a snack sizes zippy to freeze and remove from the freezer as needed. Handy AND healthy. Enjoy!

My only changes were to finely dice the onion instead of slice it (to give the sauce a more salsa-like texture), and to use a red restaurant-style salsa instead of salsa verde. Oh, and I also seasoned the raw chicken with creole seasoning salt before I put it in the pan. Turned out so good, seriously. My husband loved it, especially paired with yooper's (Recipe #21843), so much that he said it was one of the best meals I've ever made for him!

clause: I have a very similar recipe that I have used for longer than I like to remember.
review:
I have a very similar recipe that I have used for longer than I like to remember. PLEASE don't tell the folks to use your favorite beer. I knew of a woman that used her husbands favorite beer and it was a disaster. None and I repeat NONE of the lite beers are worth bringing home when it come to baking. A good dark beer that is let come to room temp( living in Pennsylvania now I have come to like Yuengling either Black and Tan or Porter) I also use it at room temp. Using beer cold shocks your mix and you don't get the same rise. Good luck and keep them cards and letters coming.
Cap'n Jack

clause: Very good salad.
review: Very good salad. The dressing was made in the morning and placed in the refrigerator until dinner time. The cranberries were frozen and after being rinsed under water were tossed into the Vita-Mix along with the other dressing ingredients except for the oil. The oil was slowly drizzled in. This produced a very creamy dressing. The salad was a mixture of baby greens, thinly sliced red onion in place of the shallot, a handful of dried cranberries and crumbled feta. Something I would make again. Made for Aussie Swap.

forgot to add the vanilla that someone else recommended, next time...

clause: Great recipe.
review:
Great recipe. I used only 1 tsp yeast. Most recipes call for way too much yeast. I had a great rise with 1 tsp and no overwhelming yeasty taste.
I also made this vegan by using almond milk. I used all whole wheat flour. I decreased the sugar because I read in other reviews that it was too sweet, but I wish I had added it all in, because I noticed it needed a little more sweetness.
At any rate, this is a really fantastic recipe and I'll make it again. Thanks for posting this!

clause: Creamy, rich, and lemony, with a very smooth texture.
review: Creamy, rich, and lemony, with a very smooth texture. I followed the recipe exactly except that I couldn't find hazelnut biscotti so I used almond biscotti dipped in bittersweet chocolate. The instructions were easy to follow and the taste was pretty good, but the crust came out kind of soggy and the lemon flavor was much more pronounced than I would have hoped. The strong citrus flavor combined with the texture of this cake reminded us of key lime pie more than anything. Thanks for sharing though. It was definately worth a try.

clause: These are the first oatmeal cookies I have baked that I liked.
review: These are the first oatmeal cookies I have baked that I liked. My only suggestion would be to make sure you boil the raisins WAY ahead of time to give them time to cool. It seems like common sense, but the first time I tried them, it was late at night and I needed them for the next day. I poured the raisin liquid in the cream mixture immediately after it finished and it melted the cream mixture and the cookies were terrible. I did let them cool for the second batch (the next day when I was a little more alert) and they went off without a hitch. Also, it didn't specify quick-cooking oats or the regular kind, but quick-cooking works great. Great recipe!

review: Great. I have had to try this salmon using lavender as the onyl herb in the sauce. And it was fantastic. The combination of honey with lavender did it for me. The sweetnes of the honey bringsout the lavender flavour so well. I used Worcester sauce. Next time I will try it with tamarind paste, which might brings out the flavours even better. The recipe is very easy to make and the sauce is the hit. I have made a fish portion for two, but make the whole amount of sauce. It is so delicious that I have dipped in some bread to get also the last drop of it. I have basted the salmon frequently to have much of the sauce on the fish. 10 minutes and the fish is flaky. I baked it a little shorter (about 7 minutes9; but that's just a personal favorite. This recipe is different, your guests will be surprised and ask you for the recipe of this unusual but delicate salmon.
